rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic eloquence contains intended subtleties calibrated to what its challengers can understand, and these details form part of its miraculous force.
rows.anchor: في كون القرآن معجزا وملحوظة للمتحدين به على مقدار ما يبلغ إليه بيان المبين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a divine hadith, transmitted by Muslim and the four Sunan collections, in which God answers the servant's phrases in al-Fatiha and shares the central petition between them.
rows.anchor: رواه مسلم والأربعة عن أبي هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith shows al-Fatiha is arranged in three sections, an instance of the rhetorical art of balanced division.
rows.anchor: في هذا الحديث تنبيه على ما في نظم فاتحة الكتاب من خصوصية التقسيم إذ قسم الفاتحة ثلاثة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition at the worship-and-help petition is a graceful bridge because it mixes the preceding and following sections.
rows.anchor: محسن التخلص في قوله فإذا قال : إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses paronomasia, illustrated by the paired forms yanhawna and yanʾawna in one phrase.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن مراعاة التجنيس في غير ما آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also uses antithesis, as in the paired verbs misguides and guides in the same statement.
rows.anchor: فإنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran explicitly calls attention to its parables and their capacity to prompt reflection among people who understand.
rows.anchor: يضرب الله الأمثال للناس وما يعقلها إلا العالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iltifat shifts from one mode of speaking, address, or third-person reference to another; the shift itself is eloquent and a fitting subtle connection makes it a rhetorical art.
rows.anchor: الالتفات وهو نقل الكلام من أحد طرق التكلم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni called iltifat Arabic bravery because the change renews the listener's attention.
rows.anchor: وسماه ابن جني شجاعة العربية لأن ذلك التغيير يجدد نشاط السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs highly prized simile and metaphor, and Quranic examples such as the head bursting into gray hair, the wings of humility, and night being stripped from day surpassed their eloquence.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في القرآن من التشبيه والاستعارة ما أعجز العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs valued completeness of likeness and especially the precaution that prevents an objection; Quranic descriptions of rivers clarify that their water, milk, wine, and honey lack unpleasant qualities.
rows.anchor: أنهار من ماء غير آسن وأنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين

words: أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُۥ جَنَّةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden destroyed by a fiery whirlwind is an extended illustrative simile, completing the likeness so the loss feels especially devastating.
rows.anchor: التمثيلية في قوله تعالى ) أيود أحدكم أن تكون له جنة من نخيل وأعناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp-niche parable supplies clarifying qualities that intensify the light and beautify the subject through the likeness.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ) مثل نوره كمشكاة ( إلى قوله ) يكاد زيتها يضيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic phrasing carries conventional compositional meaning, rhetorical meaning, and implicit meaning inferred from contextual clues; its wording is unusually rich in information and signification.
rows.anchor: إن نظم القرآن مبني على وفرة الإفادة وتعدد الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Implicit meanings are rarer in eloquent speech but frequent in the Quran, including ellipsis of a quoted saying, a described noun, or an adjective.
rows.anchor: وهذه الدلالة قليلة في كلام البلغاء وكثرت في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preface aims to sketch how the Quran is miraculous and to show its eloquence and literary subtleties, which opened new horizons for Arabic literature and thought.
rows.anchor: ثم ترى منها بلاغة القرآن ولطائف أدبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier researchers often mixed the study of Quranic inimitability with its literary eloquence or neglected the latter, although that inquiry belongs among tafsir's introductions.
rows.anchor: وكنت أرى الباحثين ممن تقدمني يخلطون هذين الغرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tafsir is incomplete unless it explains rhetorical subtleties and Arabic usage in proportion to its scope; otherwise the exegete is only a translator.
rows.anchor: لا يعد تفسيره لمعاني القرآن بالغا حد الكمال في غرضه ما لم يكن مشتملا على بيان دقائق من وجوه البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most tafsirs neglect this aim; he names al-Zajjaj and Ibn Atiyya among the less expansive, al-Kashshaf among the expansive, and exempts works focused on legal rulings, while noting discussions by Ismail b. Ishaq and Ibn al-Arabi.
rows.anchor: فمن أعجب ما نراه خلو معظم التفاسير عن الاهتمام بالوصول إلى هذا الغرض الأسمى إلا عيون التفاسير

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الباقلاني
rows.claim: Al-Baqillani's account grounds the prophetic mission in the Quran, the enduring public miracle whose binding proof remains from its revelation until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وخلاصة القول فيه أن رسالة نبينا عليه الصلاة والسلام بنيت على معجزة القرآن وإن كان قد أيد بعد ذلك بمعجزات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other prophetic miracles occurred at particular times, circumstances, and audiences, and were transmitted at differing levels; the Quran is a general miracle for all generations.
rows.anchor: فأما القرآن فهو معجزة عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran repeatedly challenged the Arabs to produce a comparable surah or ten surahs; its explicit record that they would fail was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: تتحدى العرب بأن يأتوا بسورة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: History confirms the challengers' inability: despite a long period in disbelief, they produced no matching surah and instead turned to armed resistance.
rows.anchor: فالتحدي متواتر وعجز المتحدين أيضا متواتر بشهادة التاريخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes have differed over whether taʾwil is identical to tafsir, narrower, or distinct from it.
rows.anchor: وقد جرت عادة المفسرين بالخوض في بيان معنى التأويل

rows.speaker: ثعلب وابن الأعرابي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Thalab, Ibn al-Arabi, and Abu Ubayda equate taʾwil with tafsir; this also appears to be al-Raghib's view.
rows.anchor: ذهب ثعلب وابن الأعرابي وأبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Another view assigns tafsir to the apparent meaning and taʾwil to ambiguous passages.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعل التفسير للمعنى الظاهر والتأويل للمتشابه

rows.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
rows.claim: A Usuli definition treats taʾwil as moving a word from its apparent sense to another possible sense on the basis of evidence; extracting a bird from an egg is tafsir, while extracting a believer from an unbeliever is taʾwil.
rows.anchor: التأويل صرف اللفظ عن ظاهر معناه إلى معنى آخر محتمل لدليل فيكون هنا بالمعنى الأصولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are terminological conventions, but language and transmitted usage support the first view: taʾwil returns a statement to its intended meaning, like tafsir, especially in detailed explanation of a subtle meaning.
rows.anchor: إلا أن اللغة والآثار تشهد للقول الأول

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Asha's line uses taʾwil for the gradual unfolding of love, like a young spring camel growing until it has a companion; Abu Ubayda glosses the image this way.
rows.anchor: على أنها كانت تأول حبها تأول ربعي السقاب فأصحبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Quranic phrase about people awaiting its taʾwil, the word means the clarification that was intended.
rows.anchor: أي ينتظرون إلا بيانه الذي هو المراد منه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for Ibn Abbas to be given understanding of religion and taught taʾwil, meaning comprehension of the Quran's meanings.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه لأبن عباس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet said the supplication of glorification, praise, lordship, and forgiveness while bowing, describing this as acting on the Quran.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في ركوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha's phrase yataʾawwal al-Quran explicitly means that the Prophet acted on the verse's apparent meaning, not that he read it as signaling the approaching end of his mission.
rows.anchor: صريح في أنه فسر الآية بالظاهر منها

rows.speaker: عمر وابن عباس
rows.claim: Umar and Ibn Abbas understood the cited Quranic passage as indicating that the prophetic mission was nearing its end and the Prophet's departure was approaching.
rows.anchor: الذي فهمه منها عمر وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's novel style overwhelmed even hostile rhetoricians, including converts Labid, Kab ibn Zuhayr, and al-Nabigha al-Jadi, as well as the stubborn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: المعاندين عن معارضته ولم يسعهم إلا الإذعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Quran legislates, educates, and teaches, it appropriately places as many needed and rhetorically apt meanings as possible into concise wording, beyond ordinary eloquent speech.
rows.anchor: لكونه كتاب تشريع وتأديب وتعليم كان حقيقا بأن يودع فيه من المعاني والمقاصد أكثر ما تحتمله الآلفاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran can intend a primary, higher meaning together with a secondary, lower meaning, provided the lower sense supplements rather than replaces the higher one; the senses may differ in likelihood or clarity.
rows.anchor: إذا كان المعنى الأعلى مقصودا وكان ما هو أدنى منه مرادا معه لا مرادا دونه سواء كانت دلالة التركيب عليها متساوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean either that the killers were not certain they killed him or that the Christians who disputed his killing lacked certain knowledge and misunderstood it.
rows.anchor: أي ما تيقنوا قتله ولكن توهموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the prison verse, both dhikr and rabb carry two meanings, allowing multiple readings of who forgot what and whom the lord refers to.
rows.anchor: ففي كل من كلمة ) ذكر ( و ) ربه ( معنيان

words: معاذ الله إنه ربي أحسن مثواي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rabb in Joseph's statement also admits two meanings.
rows.anchor: ففي لفظ ) رب ( معنيان

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri read أباه with bāʾ instead of إياه with yāʾ, creating uncertainty about who made the promise.
rows.anchor: فنشأ احتمال فيمن هو الواعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Quran comes from the One whose knowledge encompasses everything, every familiar meaning its eloquent constructions can bear is presumed intended unless strong legal, linguistic, or contextual evidence prevents it.
rows.anchor: ما لم يمنع من ذلك مانع صريح أو غالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran guidance for the whole community and urged reflection and interpretive effort, as shown by commands to fear God as able, refer matters to qualified authorities, and recognize clear signs in learned hearts.
rows.anchor: ودعاهم إلى تدبره وبذل الجهد في استخراج معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree the Quran is authoritative for Islamic law, while they dispute transmitted reports over authentication criteria and uneven access; the Quran is their strongest common reference in disagreement.
rows.anchor: على أن القرآن هو الحجة العامة بين علماء الإسلام لا يختلفون في كونه حجة شريعتهم وإن اختلفوا في حجية ما عداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hafs transmission of Asim is common across the eastern Islamic lands and many other countries, while Abu Amr's reading is used in Sudan near Egypt.
rows.anchor: البلاد المصرية والهند وباكستان وتركيا والأفغان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's description of its stories as the best indicates that they serve a higher purpose than entertainment, refreshment, or astonishment at events.
rows.anchor: أن القصص القرآنية لم تسق مساق الإحماض وتجديد النشاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qissa is news of an event absent from the one reporting it, so accounts of events contemporaneous with revelation, such as Muslim battles, are not technically Quranic stories.
rows.anchor: الخبر عن حادثة غائبة عن المخبر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of qissa is qiṣas with kasra on the first qaf; qaṣaṣ with fatḥa names the narrated report and is a verbal noun used for its object.
rows.anchor: وجمع القصة قصص بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic stories offer many lessons and communal benefits, select each story's noblest material, and omit the rest to avoid telling stories for amusement.
rows.anchor: إن في تلك القصص لعبرا جمة وفوائد للأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories are dispersed among surahs and placed in contexts suited to their benefits, making them reminders and admonitions closer to preaching than to a chronological history book.
rows.anchor: بل كانت مفرقة موزعة على مقامات تناسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narratives placed in their fitting contexts gain the force of proof and explanation while serving the Quran's original purposes, including legislation and its applications.
rows.anchor: سوقها في مناسباتها يكسبها صفتين : صفة البرهان وصفة التبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden story is concise: the brothers' reminder is narrated where they see the ruined garden, not during their earlier plotting or morning call to gather.
rows.anchor: فقد حكيت مقالته هذه في موقع تذكيره أصحابه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase they raced to the door omits the master's arrival, knocking, and their rush to open it; Joseph fled to escape the woman's plot, while she hurried to accuse him first.
rows.anchor: فقد طوي ذكر حضور سيدها وطرقه الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first benefit is that Quranic knowledge of prophets and earlier peoples challenged the People of the Book, broke their objections, and ended their portrayal of Muslims as an unlearned nation; earlier exegetes had not noted this benefit.
rows.anchor: فكان اشتمال القرآن على تلك القصص التي لا يعلمها إلا الراسخون في العلم من أهل الكتاب تحديا عظيما لأهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab is originally a generic, unrestricted noun or a known referent; with the latter sense it names the Quran's verses.
rows.anchor: أنزل عليك الكتاب منه آيات محكمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ayah is a portion of Quranic text, whether complete by explicit wording, understood by ellipsis, or counted by inclusion.
rows.anchor: هي مقدار من القرآن مركب ولو تقديرا أو إلحاقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implicit construction in mدهامتان supplies a subject, while al-Fajr implies an oath verb, as in I swear by the dawn.
rows.anchor: فقولي ولو تقديرا لإدخال قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some disconnected opening letters are counted as verses in the codices, while Alif Lam Ra, Alif Lam Mim Ra, and Ta Sin are excluded; this is an established, transmitted convention with no evident distinction.
rows.anchor: فقد عد أكثرها في المصاحف آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Quranic portions ayat is a Quranic innovation, as shown in its descriptions of the book's verses.
rows.anchor: هذه الأجزاء آيات هو من مبتكرات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ayah is a sign of revelation because its composition reaches the highest eloquence; verses together also prove the Quran is divine, since human eloquent speakers failed the challenge to match a surah.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت آية لأنها دليل على أنها موحى بها من عند الله إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنها تشتمل على ما هو من الحد الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Torah and Gospel clauses should not be called ayat, since Hebrew and Aramaic do not share the Quran's distinctive linguistic quality.
rows.anchor: فلذا لا يحق لجمل التوراة والإنجيل أن تسمى آيات إذ ليست فيها هذه الخصوصية في اللغة العبرانية والآرامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the report about the stoning of two Jews, the narrator's phrase ayat al-rajm is an analogical expression for a Torah passage, used because he lacked another name for it.
rows.anchor: فذلك تعبير غلب على لسان الراوي على وجه المشاكلة التقديرية تشبيها بجمل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse boundaries are transmitted from the Prophet; varying reports about some boundaries reflect latitude in where those verses end and the next begins, and the Companions knew the divisions.
rows.anchor: وتحديد مقادير الآيات مروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد تختلف الرواية في بعض الآيات وهو محمول على التخيير في حد تلك الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An authentic hadith calls al-Fatiha the seven oft-repeated, meaning its seven verses.
rows.anchor: قلت وفي الحديث الصحيح أن فاتحة الكتاب السبع المثاني أي السبع الآيات

words: إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith about reciting the last ten of al-Imran refers to the ten verses beginning with the signs in creation and ending with the surah.
rows.anchor: وهي الآيات التي أولها ( إن في خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur announces that the Quran has distinctive stylistic innovations which he proceeds to enumerate.
rows.anchor: هذا وللقرآن مبتكرات تميز بها نظمه عن بقية كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran departs from both poetry and ordinary oratory, using a novel form of a book meant to be preserved and recited; this is one aspect of its inimitability.
rows.anchor: فمنها أنه جاء على أسلوب يخالف الشعر لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic sentences state carefully delimited propositions and rules rather than loose generalities or unrestricted statements, unlike Arab usage that often ignored rare cases.
rows.anchor: جاء بالجمل الدالة على معان مفيدة محررة شأن الجمل العلمية والقواعد التشريعية

words: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification excluding those with disabilities exemplifies the Quran's precise delimitation of a general statement.
rows.anchor: مثاله قوله تعالى ) لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون

words: ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example shows that desire can be praiseworthy when a person's desire follows divine guidance.
rows.anchor: فبين أن الهوى قد يكون محمودا إذا كان هوى المرء عن هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that humanity is in loss is explicitly qualified by the following exception for believers, exemplifying precise wording.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran introduced systematic division and topic classification into Arabic discourse, a practice al-Kashshaf had hinted at.
rows.anchor: طريقة التبويب والتصنيف وقد أومأ إليها في الكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic narrative vividly depicts paradise, punishment, and states of affairs; this strongly affected Arabs because narrative was nearly absent from Arabic literature, apart from rare poetic episodes such as al-Nabigha's snake story.
rows.anchor: وقد كان لذلك تأثير عظيم على نفوس العرب إذ كان فن القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran reshapes reported speech into its own miraculous Arabic style; reported words convey meaning rather than exact wording, so the inimitability belongs to the Quran, not the quoted speakers.
rows.anchor: فهو إذا حكى أقوالا غير عربية صاغ مدلولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also adapts names in its narratives for eloquence, changing Saul to Talut and Terah, Abraham's father, to Azar.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل حكاية الأسماء الواقعة في القصص فإن القرآن يغيرها إلى ما يناسب حسن مواقعها في الكلام
